title: Reword "a sound plan refused": the refused reply has no retained review.
comment:
**Reword "a sound plan refused": the refused reply has no retained review.**

The refused Daniel 7:10 reply exists only in `provider.ndjson`. The release has no `review-daniel-7-10.json`, and `scene-daniel-7-10.json` holds only the error. The release `README.md` is more careful and says the scene fields "would have met the declared criterion".

The reply's `primarySubject` also reads "Radiance and fire seated above an unoccupied throne". The planner instructions say to describe an unoccupied seat, not a seated presence. This wording makes "sound" a stronger claim than the evidence supports.

Replace "a sound plan" with wording such as "a plan that appeared to meet its declared criterion on agent reading, with no retained review".

title: Document the pinned base worktree and generated manifest input.
comment:
**Document the pinned base worktree and generated manifest input.**

`verify.mts` hashes every path in `sha256.json`. The release directory is absent from `296df4219e61da29d31052d7d9b348e4c75fd0fd`, and `works/bible-web/work.json` is also absent until `npm run works:import` generates it. Other manifest paths, including `works/bible-web/brief.json`, match the base. A release-directory-only overlay is therefore insufficient. Later changes to manifest-listed source files also fail the audit.

<details>
<summary>Suggested README update</summary>

```diff
 ## Offline audit
 
-Run `npm run works:import`, then:
+Run the audit from a worktree at `296df4219e61da29d31052d7d9b348e4c75fd0fd`. This base commit does not contain the release directory. From a checkout that contains the release artifacts, create the audit worktree and overlay the release directory:
+
+git worktree add --detach ../grounded-plan-audit 296df4219e61da29d31052d7d9b348e4c75fd0fd
+mkdir -p ../grounded-plan-audit/llm/releases
+cp -R llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check ../grounded-plan-audit/llm/releases/
+cd ../grounded-plan-audit
+
+Keep all other paths listed in `sha256.json` at the recorded base revision. Run `npm run works:import` to generate `works/bible-web/work.json`, then:
 
 ```sh
 npx tsx llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check/verify.mts
 ```
```

</details>

   
<repository_evidence>
<fact source="llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check/verify.mts:15-18">The script executes `for (const [file, digest] of Object.entries(manifest)) assert.equal(hash(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, file))), digest, file);`, then executes `assert.deepEqual(sources(), before.sources); assert.deepEqual(final.sources, before.sources);` and reads pinned files with `git show`.</fact>
<fact source="llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check/sha256.json; shell output shell-output-85riU8">The manifest lists release files and paths outside the release directory. The base commit matches the manifest for `src/lib/engine/*`, `src/lib/reading-pass/*`, `convex/*`, `works/bible-web/brief.json`, and `styles/*`. `works/bible-web/work.json` is missing from the base.</fact>
<fact source="llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check/README.md:46-54">The README gives the import and verification commands but does not explain how to obtain the uncommitted release artifacts while retaining the pinned base worktree.</fact>
<inference source="llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check/verify.mts:15-18; llm/releases/2026-10-23-grounded-plan-check/sha256.json; shell output shell-output-85riU8">A base worktree with only the release directory overlaid cannot satisfy the manifest until `works/bible-web/work.json` is generated, and a later modification to another manifest-listed path can fail the audit.</inference>
<fact source="review comparison">The full PR comparison base is unavailable, so the inspected source does not establish when this behavior was introduced.</fact>
</repository_evidence>
</verification_result>
